content: There’s something about a movie like The Room, Troll 2, or Fateful Findings that I find irresistible. These sorts of “so bad they’re good” films are marvelous curiosities where ambition far outstrips resources, ability, and self-awareness to become something much greater than the sum of their parts. Champagne and Bullets (also released as GetEven and Road to Revenge) is a film on par with those classics of outsider cinema.  The movie is almost entirely the work of one man, John De Hart. Hart wrote, directed, and stars as Rick Bode in the film. He even performs a musical number early in the proceedings — The bizarre “Shimmy Slide.” During the performance, Hart, who was reportedly pumped full of painkillers after throwing out his back, is stiff and looks around the room as if he’s only performing under threat of violence. And somehow, this lifeless performance of a cringy country rocker isn’t the most awkward scene in the movie. [Media: https://youtu.be/zN2UuGfGr8k] The relationships and interactions between characters in Champagne and Bullets are just as inexplicable and unnatural as those in The Room. Bode and his partner Huck Finney are cops who lose their badges five minutes into the movie. This precipitates the alarmingly quick mental decline of Finney, who is also going through a divorce after discovering his wife has been sleeping around. He fires a handgun through his bills, drinks bleach to get out of prison, and seemingly starts a cult. Oh, and speaking of cults, a good portion of the plot revolves around the reemergence of Bode’s old girlfriend Cindy, who is fleeing a satanic coven that “sacrificed a human baby.” While ostensibly an action film, the fight scenes are few and far between, and staged with all the believability of a theme park stunt show. Hart seemed far more interested in cramming in as much gratuitous nudity as possible. There are three uncomfortably long sex scenes with costar Pamela Bryant, who plays Cindy, all set to songs sung by Hart. In total, they take up 12 minutes of runtime in a movie that is only 90 minutes long. One scene that takes place in a jacuzzi apparently even led Hart’s girlfriend at the time to break up with him. (Warning: One scene not involving Hart and Bryant does depict a sexual assault.) If you’re a fan of bad movies, cult classics, or the podcast How Did This Get Made, you owe it to yourself to go watch Champagne and Bullets. It’s available on Hoopla, Amazon Prime, and Tubi.

chineseContent: 像《房间》、《巨魔2》或《命运的发现》这样的电影有一些让我无法抗拒的东西。这类“虽然糟糕但也很好”的电影是令人惊叹的好奇心，其中的野心远远超过资源、能力和自我意识，成为比各个部分的总和更伟大的东西。 《香槟与子弹》（也以《GetEven》和《复仇之路》发行）是一部与局外人电影的经典电影相媲美的电影。  这部电影几乎完全是约翰·德哈特一个人的作品。哈特自编自导并在影片中饰演瑞克·博德。他甚至在演出初期表演了一段音乐剧——奇异的“Shimmy Slide”。据报道，在表演期间，哈特在摔倒后被注射了大量止痛药，他的身体僵硬，环顾房间四周，好像他只是在暴力威胁下表演。不知怎的，这位卑鄙的乡村摇滚歌手毫无生气的表演并不是电影中最尴尬的场景。 [媒体：https://youtu.be/zN2UuGfGr8k] 《香槟》和《子弹》中人物之间的关系和互动就像《房间》中一样莫名其妙、不自然。博德和他的搭档哈克·芬尼是警察，他们在电影开场五分钟就失去了徽章。这导致芬尼的精神迅速衰退，令人震惊，在发现妻子到处乱搞后，芬尼也正在经历离婚。他用手枪射击他的账单，喝漂白剂以逃离监狱，并且似乎开始了一个邪教。哦，说到邪教，情节的很大一部分围绕着博德的旧女友辛迪的重新出现展开，她正在逃离一个“牺牲了人类婴儿”的撒旦集会。虽然表面上是一部动作片，但打斗场面却很少而且间隔很远，而且上演时充满了主题公园特技表演的可信度。哈特
